raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose This PR improves the performance and correctness of the `moeTopK` kernel. 1. **Performance Optimization:** Optimized `indices` access by caching prior winning experts in Shared Memory. This reduces redundant Global Memory reads, which is highly effective when `k` is large. 2. **Bugfix (Logic)**: Fixed a potential bug where the `start_expert` offset was not applied consistently during index comparisons. This issue was previously hidden because existing implementations only used `start_expert=0`. It appears the Expert Parallelism (EP) logic in this kernel was effectively dead logic. To simplify the codebase and prevent future confusion, I removed the `start_expert` and `end_expert` parameters entirely. 3. **Bugfix (Type):** Replaced hardcoded `int` with the correct template type `IndType`. 4. **Refactor:** Unified the mixed usage of `block_row` and `blockIdx.x` to `block_row` for better readability. 5. **Refactor:** Improved code clarity by explicitly setting `inp_kvp.value = -1.f` when an expert is already found in prior iterations. This clearly indicates that the expert is being "skipped" rather than re-assigned. ## Test Plan 1. Modified existing kernel benchmark: `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_fused_topk.py` ``` num_tokens_range = [128, 512, 2048, 8192, 16384] num_experts_range = [137, 513, 768, 1234] topk_range = [8, 16, 32, 64] ``` - Expanded the range of num_tokens to simulate high-load serving environments. - Included non-power-of-two num_experts values. - Increased top_k values to evaluate the efficiency of the new Shared Memory caching logic. 3. Profile with NVIDIA Nsight Compute (NCU) to measure hardware-level memory workload and latency changes. ``` ncu --set full --kernel-name moeTopK -c 1 -o moe_profile_result -f python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_fused_topk.py ``` ## Test Result **Nsight Compute (NCU) Profiling Results:** | Metric | **Before** | **After** | **Diff** | | ------------------------ | ---------- | --------- | ------------- | | **Duration** | 16.10 us | 15.58 us | **-3.18%** | | **Elapsed Cycles** | 26,953 | 26,116 | **-3.11%** | | **L2 Transactions** | 9,170 | 8,580 | **-6.43%** | | **Shared Load/Store** | 108,994 | 120,435 | **+10.50%** | | **Memory Throughput** | 39.10% | 36.66% | **-6.23%** | | **Dynamic Smem / Block** | 0 Bytes | 32 Bytes | **+32 Bytes** | ---
Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. - [ ] (Optional) Release notes update. If your change is user facing, please update the release notes draft in the [Google Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1YyVqrgX4gHTtrstbq8oWUImOyPCKSGnJ7xtTpmXzlRs/edit?tab=t.0).

## Code Review

This pull request refactors the moeTopK CUDA kernel by removing expert range parameters and introducing dynamic shared memory to store and access indices. This change optimizes the process of checking for previously selected experts. A review comment suggests further optimizing the expert deduplication loop by adding a break statement once a match is found to eliminate redundant iterations as the number of experts increases.
I didn't use `break` because of warp divergence. It provides 0% speedup for $K \le 32$ while adding branch overhead.
